summary: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under F. E. L. Priestley and doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held an attested post at the University of Toronto in 1991.

Leonard Swidler was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from St. Norbert College, Marquette, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later serving as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).
Leonard Woolley was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He was educated at St John's School, Leatherhead (circa 1893–1899) and New College (circa 1899–1903).
Leonard Zwilling was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and completed his studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1976.

Leonard van der Kuijp is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. and D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He taught at the University of Washington and became Department Chair at Harvard University in 1995.
Leonid Kulikov is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held an attested post at Leiden University in 2007 and serves on the faculty at Ghent University, attested in 2026.

Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University, Willamette University, the University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale from 1956 and as an anthropology curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (circa 1956–1993).

Leopold von Schroeder was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer, as well as at Tübingen, Jena, and under Rudolf von Roth. He held professorships at the universities of Tartu, Innsbruck (1896), and Vienna (1899).

Leslie S. Kawamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther and served as a professor, later Professor of Buddhist Studies, at the University of Calgary from circa 1976 to 2011.

Levi McLaughlin specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Princeton University and the University of Tokyo under Susumu Shimazono, and has served as an associate professor at North Carolina State University since 2012.
Lewin Bentham Bowring was an Indologist and historian. He served as Chief Commissioner for the Government of Mysore from circa 1862 to 1870 and held a post at the University of Mysore.

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He has held research and teaching posts at the British Museum, Freie Universität Berlin, the University of Munich, and the University of Bonn.

Lewis Hodous was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Case Western Reserve University, Hartford Seminary, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He served as president of Fukien Union Theological Seminary and later taught at Hartford Seminary (1917–1945).

Lewis Lancaster is a Buddhist studies scholar and sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, and as president of the University of the West.

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991) and as secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), becoming Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center in 2000.

Lhakpa Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He has served as a professor at Tibet University and as Assistant Professor of Tibetan Language and Literature at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 2026.

Li-ching Chang was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who taught Mandarin Chinese at the University of Washington, Tunghai University, Bryn Mawr College, Harvard University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Swarthmore College.
Liang Cai is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied under Daniel Boucher. She held a post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas, attested in 2014.

Libbie Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. She held an attested post teaching Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto in 2020.
